A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical framework and retain corresponding results and experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: Appendix D reports original synthetic experiments on gradient consistency, Gibbs equilibrium and concentration, and multimodal misalignment.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain the synthetic experiments and report original MS-COCO checkpoint evaluations and controlled caption-corruption experiments.

M1.justification: The analyzed InfoNCE objectives, kernels, and synthetic training procedures remain substantively unchanged. The added CLIP probing and projection-head fine-tuning are validation procedures, not newly proposed learning methods.

E1.justification: V2 extends the synthetic-only coverage to MS-COCO image-text retrieval and training with same-category caption corruption. The original Gaussian-mixture, spherical-particle, and latent-angle settings remain, including all eight misalignment scales in Appendix F.3.

E2.justification: The large-batch gradient reference and Gibbs equilibrium remain the reference comparisons. The nine OpenCLIP checkpoints in v2 Table 2 are systems examined to test the theory; no competing algorithm or loss is newly evaluated against a proposed method.

E3.justification: V2 adds frozen-checkpoint evaluation on 5,000 validation images with up to five captions each, bidirectional Recall@1, and several distributional diagnostics. Its corruption experiment introduces five corruption probabilities and projection-head/logit-scale fine-tuning with frozen backbones. The existing synthetic protocols are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F.4 adds a controlled real-data sensitivity study testing whether semantically plausible caption mispairing enlarges the modality gap. Separate retrieval-direction analyses test whether the observed retrieval-gap relationship is an averaging artifact, while multiple discrepancy metrics check its dependence on the diagnostic.

E5.justification: Synthetic experiments retain 20 seeds, and v2 newly identifies seed 0 for qualitative displays. The gradient caption changes from standard error to standard deviation. Conversely, Appendix F.2 changes cap-mass reporting to standard error while Figure 2a still says standard deviation, leaving that uncertainty scaling inconsistent.

E6.justification: V2 adds nine checkpoints' retrieval and discrepancy scores in Table 2 and new corruption results. For example, Appendix F.4.2 reports ResNet-50 AvgR@1 falling from 0.398 to 0.226 and centroid gap rising from 0.845 to 1.081 as corruption probability increases from 0 to 1. V1 contains no corresponding real-data results.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and inheritance results survive renumbering and relocation. Limited mathematical revisions include Remark 2.1's pointwise-normalization extension and Appendix B.3's density-floor inequality. New Eq. (28) introduces an erroneous temperature factor in the free-energy/KL identity, conflicting with v1 Eq. (43) and v2 Eq. (32).

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the modality gap from a structural necessity to something symmetric InfoNCE can favor under conditional heterogeneity in the analyzed regime. Contribution (iv) now emphasizes empirical validation instead of parametric inheritance, although the inheritance results remain in Appendix C.

C2.justification: V2 adds an interpretation of early gap growth as sensitivity to pairing quality and expands the finite-temperature positivity discussion. It removes v1 Remark 4.3's sign-inconsistent barrier explanation. Most limitations remain in condensed form, although Appendix F.3 retains categorical necessity language despite the qualified main claims.

D1.justification: V2 documents COCO selection and corruption procedures, frozen components, and fine-tuning settings: AdamW, learning rate 10^-5, weight decay 0.05, batch size 256, and 5,000 steps. It also clarifies qualitative-run sampling. However, v1's project-code access footnote is removed; the PDFs do not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands positioning against training-dynamics analyses, variational perspectives, and distribution-matching or sigmoid objectives, including Sun, Liao, Calder and Lee, Yin, and Zhai. Several earlier diagnostic and extension references disappear. The Liu 2024-to-2026 change concerns the same Beyond DAGs work, not a new citation.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, theory sections gain a new subsection structure, and corollaries and stability statements move to reorganized appendices. V2 adds repeated proof-intuition explanations, distinguishes measures from densities more explicitly, and replaces the main limitations section with empirical validation.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned with geometric landscapes. Synthetic plots are relocated, combined, and selectively repeated in the main text; gradient curves share panels and joint-angle heatmaps adopt logarithmic coloring. V2 also adds notation and checkpoint tables plus COCO overview and directional-result figures.

improvement.justification: The COCO observations and controlled corruption study improve empirical grounding, while clearer organization and qualified main claims improve accessibility and calibration. These gains are tempered by the removed code-access link, inconsistent uncertainty labels, and the erroneous factor in Eq. (28). The revision provides a limited net improvement without substantially strengthening the retained theoretical guarantees.
